teaser.text: Qualcomm makes the technology that helps devices compute and connect, and it also licenses inventions used by cellular networks. Its business is easiest to understand as two linked flows: it sells engineered platforms, then earns separate fees when manufacturers use its patents.

stock.meta_description: Qualcomm stock forecast: bear, base and bull cases, cash generation, and the valuation behind the range.
stock.opening: The weighted October 2027 price is $142.82, a 16% loss including dividends. The thesis is simple: Qualcomm’s upside depends on turning its pipeline into repeated, profitable shipments without weakening the cash engine that already works.

blocks.heading: Where could Qualcomm's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to a weak first year, followed by recovery. The weighted October 2027 price is $142.82, a 16% loss including dividends. It reaches $174.23 in October 2028, a 4% gain. By October 2029, it reaches $224.14, a 35% gain.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Qualcomm?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit is the main swing factor. The base case rises from $11,700 million in October 2027 to $13,230 million in October 2028. It reaches $15,120 million in October 2029. The base path uses revenue of $45,000 million at a 26% margin, then $49,000 million at 27%, and finally $54,000 million at 28%. Those margins move toward fiscal 2025’s level as data-center, automotive and IoT growth absorbs early costs.

The bear case remains below the five-year average of $11,173 million because handset pressure and weak data-center conversion persist. Its revenue rises from $40,000 million to $44,000 million, while margins stay near 20–21%. The bull case reaches $18,600 million on $62,000 million of revenue and a 30% margin, requiring repeat data-center shipments and stronger premium handset content.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Qualcomm today?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio says how much investors pay for each dollar of profit. Qualcomm trades at 20.2 times trailing earnings and 17.2 times expected earnings over the next twelve months. The trailing figure is distorted by a $5.7 billion tax benefit: an accounting reversal of an earlier allowance, not money earned from customers.

dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Qualcomm’s business, rivals, management choices, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Qualcomm pay in dividends over time?

paragraphs.text: On March 17, 2026, Qualcomm authorized another $20 billion of repurchases and raised its quarterly dividend to $0.92 per share. An authorization is permission to spend, not money already spent. The decision increases the importance of whether Qualcomm’s new businesses can replace the ownership given away in acquisitions and Amazon’s warrant.

The base dividend rises from $3.80 to $4.04 per share. The bear case holds $3.68 throughout, while the bull case reaches $4.48. The base assumes modest increases after the current $3.68 annualized rate, supported by five years of increases and fiscal 2025 free cash flow of $12,820 million.

blocks.heading: Is Qualcomm's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Across fiscal 2021–2025, most free cash flow went to dividends and buybacks. Dividends deliver cash directly. Buybacks increase each remaining share’s ownership only when the company retires more shares than it issues. That distinction matters because employee compensation, acquisitions and strategic agreements can create new shares while Qualcomm is buying others back.

Stock compensation makes conventional free cash flow look better than the ownership economics. Qualcomm recorded $2,783 million of stock compensation in FY2025. Subtracting that analytical cost leaves $10,037 million of real free cash flow. No additional cash payment occurs, but existing shareholders own a smaller share of the company.

blocks.heading: What is Qualcomm's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash left after capital spending. Its 6.9% yield falls to 5.4% under the stated “real” adjustment, while the dividend yield is 2.1%. Price to book is 6.7 times, but internally developed patents and engineering knowledge are not fully recorded as assets.

blocks.heading: What has Qualcomm guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: QCT is Qualcomm’s chip business, while “non-handset” means chips sold outside smartphones. Management wants non-handset products to become at least half of QCT revenue in fiscal 2027 and to grow at least 60% that year, including data-center products. The first test is therefore size; the second is genuine sales momentum.

The nearer data-center target is $5 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027. Two hyperscalers—operators of enormous cloud-computing networks—are each expected to contribute at least $1 billion through custom silicon. These are chips designed for particular customers, so their schedules and purchasing decisions matter directly.

blocks.heading: Has Qualcomm kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management’s expansion promises need the same discipline. Snapdragon X laptops show that the NUVIA technology reached customers. Automotive and Internet of Things revenue grew 28% year over year in July 2026, but the broader target of US$40 billion in non-handset revenue by fiscal 2029—including data centers—remains a promise. Qualcomm’s leaders therefore look aligned with shareholders in some ways, but the final judgment rests on whether new products, restrained pay and ambitious targets produce durable returns.

blocks.heading: What do Qualcomm's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue fell to $9,947 million from $10,365 million a year earlier, while gross margin fell to 53.1%. Operating income declined to $1,626 million. A sequential decline can reflect launch timing, but year-on-year revenue and margin declines together point to a deeper problem.

The quarter also included $726 million of net gains on marketable securities, which helped net income reach $2,002 million even as operating income weakened. Cash gave the clearest warning: operating cash fell to $991 million, and free cash flow fell to $495 million. Management expected Chinese handset revenue to bottom in June, but that remains an expectation until customer sell-through, margins and cash generation improve together.
